newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Novosibirsk postpones bond repayment.
newsitem.headline: Russian Novosibirsk postpones bond repayment.

text.p: The regional administration in the Siberian city of Novosibirsk has postponed repaying an issue of 4.60 billion roubles ($859,500) of KODO municipal bonds maturing on Wednesday for two days, dealers there said.
The Novosibirsk region administration was unavailable for comment and RIF company, the local lead manager for placing KODOs, refused to comment.
"We were simply shocked when we realised looking on dark monitors of the system that there will be no repayment or trading," one dealer told Reuters.
Robert Devane, head of fixed income at Troika-Dialog brokerage in Moscow, said it appeared to be the first time a Russian municipal administration had failed to pay its bonds in time.
He said the short default would make investors more cautious in future when considering securities issued by municipalities with no previous record of servicing debt.
"We believe the effect of this default will be to stem the flow of investment funds to municipalities trying to establish municipal finance programmes," he said.
He said more developed markets with municipal bond programme had a very rich history of defaults.

In Russia 53 regions and republics, including St Petersburg, Nizny Novgorod and the republic of Tatarstan, issue municipal bonds to finance local investment programmes. But experts say many issues are not backed by real money.
Dealers said the Novosibirsk administration had suspended trading in other KODO issues until the expiring bonds had been repaid.
The administration on Monday cancelled an auction where it planned to offer three trillion roubles in a new tranche.

Konstantin Yadritinsky, SK-Finans investment company president in Novosibirsk, said the formal explanation for the default was a technical breakdown in the work of finance and tax policy department of the administration.

"Local government finance department deputy head Alexei Volkov told dealers today that the delay in repaying KODOs followed lower tax receipts into the regional budget on August 26," said Mikhail Budnov, a dealer from IKSI brokerage.
"The funds came to the regional administration account only today."
Mikhail Nagayev, a dealer from Bank Aktsept in Novosibirsk, said that RIF's president had promised to ask the regional administration to pay a penalty to investors to make up for the two-day delay.
The sum, calculated according to the refinancing rate of the Russian Central Bank, will amount to 22.00 million roubles.
